title: 3 TIMES
sub: The Mongols took Vietnam's capital three times. Each time, they withdrew.
say: The Mongols took Vietnam's capital three times. Each time, they withdrew.

sub: A Mongol army under Uriyangkhadai marches in from Yunnan, wins a battle, and takes Thăng Long. The Trần king and his court escape.
say: Twelve fifty-eight. A Mongol army under Oo-ree-yang-kha-dye marches in from Yunnan, wins a battle, and takes Tahng Long. The Chun king and his court escape.

title: SONG CHINA
sub: The Mongols do not stay. This campaign was part of their bigger war against Song China. The Trần court sends envoys and agrees to pay tribute.
say: The Mongols do not stay. This campaign was part of their bigger war against Song China. The Chun court sends envoys, and agrees to pay tribute.

sub: Now Kublai Khan rules China as the Yuan dynasty. His son Toghan invades from the north, while General Sogetu attacks from Champa in the south.
say: Twelve eighty-five. Now Kublai Khan rules China, as the Yuan dynasty. His son, Toe-gahn, invades from the north, while General Soh-geh-too attacks from Champa, in the south.

title: HOW MANY?
sub: Sources disagree wildly: from tens of thousands to half a million.
say: How big was the army? Sources disagree wildly. From tens of thousands, to half a million.

title: EMPTY CITY
sub: The Trần court leaves the capital. The Yuan army occupies empty palaces. Then the counterattack: Sogetu is killed, Toghan retreats north.
say: The Chun court leaves the capital. The Yuan army occupies empty palaces. Then the counterattack comes. Soh-geh-too is killed, and Toe-gahn retreats north.

sub: In 1287 the Yuan return. By early 1288 they hold Thăng Long a third time. Then a Vietnamese fleet destroys their grain convoy, and the army goes hungry.
say: In twelve eighty-seven, the Yuan return. By early twelve eighty-eight, they hold Tahng Long a third time. But a Vietnamese fleet destroys their grain convoy, and the army starts to go hungry.

title: BẠCH ĐẰNG
sub: In 1288 the Yuan fleet withdraws down the Bạch Đằng River, onto sharpened stakes driven into the riverbed. As the tide falls, the ships are trapped and the fleet is destroyed.
say: In twelve eighty-eight, the Yuan fleet withdraws down the Bahk Dahng River. Vietnamese forces had driven sharpened stakes into the riverbed. As the tide falls, the ships are trapped, and the fleet is destroyed.

title: TWO VIEWS
sub: Kublai demanded that the Trần king come to court in person. The Trần sent envoys and gifts, but never went. Kublai saw defiance. Later Vietnamese histories celebrate resistance.
say: Kublai demanded that the Chun king come to his court in person. The Chun kings sent envoys and gifts, but never went. Kublai treated the refusal as defiance. Later Vietnamese histories celebrate it as resistance.

sub: After the fighting, Đại Việt sent tribute and a golden statue instead of the king. The Yuan still discussed another campaign in 1293. After Kublai died in 1294, the plan was dropped.
say: So after the fighting ended, Dye Vee-et sent tribute, and a golden statue, instead of the king himself. The Yuan were still discussing another campaign in twelve ninety-three. After Kublai died in twelve ninety-four, the plan was dropped.

title: RICE & EMPIRES
sub: Winning a war and keeping the peace are different skills.
say: Winning a war, and keeping the peace, are different skills. Follow for more.
